hook: SCP-1237 is a sleep phenomenon, but the real subject of the file is how far the Foundation is prepared to go about it. The containment procedures come before the description and run long, and they are deliberately shocking: forced abortions, sterilization campaigns and sponsorship of genocide are all authorized in flat administrative language. Don't skim them; the note at the end explains why someone signed off on all of it.
whyItMatters:
Because the threat is carried in a gene, containment stops being about one object and turns into a program aimed at entire populations. It's an uncontained Keter where the anomaly feels less frightening than the policy written around it.

The file pushes the Foundation's willingness to do terrible things for the greater good about as far as it can go, and it does so without any villain monologue, only procedure.
thingsToNotice:
Taken as a list, the effects sound almost whimsical: regrown limbs, flight, the dead coming back years later, a republic quietly becoming a monarchy. The horror is in the rules: only people and places the dreamer actually knows get rewritten, and everyone else accepts the new version as how things always were while still carrying memories of the old one. The rare lucid dreamers are treated as a weapon to be aimed once at a Keter object and then killed, and the only one ever found is mentioned solely through an experiment log the file doesn't include.

The senior researcher's note admits nobody knows how much of today's world was already dreamed into shape, raises the possibility of someone dreaming the Foundation out of existence, and ends by turning sleep into the argument itself: the staff must accept sleepless nights so that nobody else is left unable to wake.
